sentences.text:
The above case is chargesheeted alleging offences punishable under Secs.323, 406, 498A r/w 34 IPC.
2.
The prosecution case is that the defacto complainant married the 1st accused and was staying in the house of the 1 st accused.
It is submitted that there was mental and physical harassment from the accused towards the defacto complainant and hence, it is alleged that the accused committed the offences alleged.

The trial court after considering the evidence adduced by the prosecution,
convicted the revision petitioners under Secs. 406 and 498A IPC.
The conviction and sentence was challenged before the Sessions Court by filing an appeal.

In the appeal, the conviction and sentence Abdul Majeed vs State Of Kerala on 9 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/26955816/
2 imposed under Sec. 406 IPC is set aside and the conviction and sentence imposed under Sec.498A IPC is upheld.

sentences.text: Aggrieved by the same, this Crl.R.P. is filed.
3. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioners and the learned counsel appearing for the 2nd respondent.
I also heard the learned Public Prosecutor.

4. When this revision petition came up for consideration, the learned counsel appearing for the revision petitioner and the 2nd respondent submitted that the entire dispute between the revision petitioners and the 2 nd respondent are settled out of court.
Admittedly, it is a matrimonial dispute and the parties settled the matter.
In such circumstances, I am of the considered opinion that the conviction and sentence imposed against the petitioners can be set aside.
Therefore, this Crl. Revision Petition is allowed.

1) The impugned judgment dated 25.04.2012 in CC No. 656/2008 on the file of the Chief Judicial Magistrate Court, Kasaragod as modified by the judgment dated 15.10.2013 in Crl.Appeal No. 82/2012 of the Additional Sessions Judge-III,
Kasaragod are set aside.
